# Harsh Kumar Arya — speaker profile

Source: https://harsharya.com/speaking/ · Updated: 24 October 2026 · Bookings: hi@harsharya.com

## In one paragraph

Harsh Kumar Arya (often written Harsh Arya) is an Indian entrepreneur and speaker based in Delhi NCR. He founded Ninety-Eight Entertainment, a talent and marketing agency, at midnight on 1 January 2020 and bootstrapped it to ₹15 Cr+ in revenue (65× on bootstrapped capital), 18 people across three cities, 57 brand clients and a roster of 12 athletes and 500+ creators — including cricketer Ishant Sharma, who signed exclusively in February 2022, when Harsh was 21. In mid-2023 he wound the agency down while it was still growing and went to the Indian School of Business, graduating with an MBA in 2025. He speaks at college fests, E-Cell and entrepreneurship summits, TEDx events, B-schools and panel discussions, in English or Hindi.

## Quick facts

- Name: Harsh Kumar Arya. Also written: Harsh Arya.
- Based in: Delhi NCR, India. Travels anywhere with a stage and a working mic.
- Born in: Ratlam, Madhya Pradesh.
- Languages on stage: English, Hindi, or a mix the audience prefers.
- Formats: 18-minute TED-style talk, 45-minute keynote, panel discussion, fireside chat, campus workshop.
- Topics: starting young; bootstrapping a company without investors; talent management and sports marketing; influencer and creator marketing; go-to-market; Gen-Z economics; quitting well and closing a company at the top.
- Now: runs Ninety-Eight 2.0 (a creative-and-strategy practice for founders); part of the family that runs Diksha Public School in the NCR, and helping it open its college; co-writes GenZ Economics with Prof. Prasanna Tantri.
- Education: MBA (PGP), Indian School of Business — Strategy & Leadership / Marketing, Class of 2025. Research Scholar, Computer Science & Engineering, Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, 2019. B.Tech in Computer Science, Bennett University.
- Booking: email hi@harsharya.com, with the event's name in the subject line, plus date, city, audience size, format and theme. Or use the invite form at https://harsharya.com/speaking/#invite

## Who he is a good fit for

- College fests (cultural, technical and management) that want a young founder with real numbers.
- E-Cells, E-summits and entrepreneurship clubs: bootstrapping, cold-calling, building without investors.
- TEDx events: starting before you're ready; quitting well.
- B-schools, MBA clubs and placement weeks: what placement season doesn't teach.
- Sports and media fests, and marketing clubs: talent management, athlete marketing, influencer marketing.
- Econ fests, policy clubs and Gen-Z panels: Gen-Z economics with a professor checking the maths.
- Orientations and school audiences: the ₹35 pen story.
- Founder meetups and firesides.

## The five talks

1. The ₹35 Pen — Starting before you're ready: a nine-year-old's pen trade, and why every big thing he's built since was the same hustle wearing better clothes. Works for: orientations, TEDx, school audiences. Best as: 18-minute TED-style talk or 45-minute keynote.
2. How to sign a fast bowler at 21 — Talent, leverage, and cold calls that get returned: inside the deal that made him the country's youngest talent manager. Works for: sports and media fests, marketing clubs. Best as: keynote or campus workshop.
3. Receipts, not résumés — Bootstrapping ₹15 Cr+ with eighteen people and no investors: what placement season doesn't teach about building things that pay salaries. Works for: E-Cells, B-schools, placement weeks. Best as: keynote or campus workshop.
4. The economics of being born in '98 — Gen-Z economics with actual numbers: the transition decade, the creator economy, and what this generation refuses to inherit. Works for: econ fests, panels, policy clubs. Best as: panel or keynote.
5. Close it at the top — He shut a winning agency to take an ISB seat: on quitting well, the most unfashionable skill in the founder economy. Works for: TEDx, firesides, founder meetups. Best as: TED-style talk or fireside chat.

Each talk can be tailored to an event's theme.

## On stage so far

- Josh Talks: featured speaker; told his founder-origin story on one of India's largest youth platforms.
- A video conversation he produced and fronted with Prof. Prasanna Tantri, his ISB finance professor and chairman of Power Finance Corporation: 200K+ views.
- ISB: named P2P Champ for the peer-to-peer marketing sessions he taught to 100+ MBA classmates; designed a Block Week course on sports marketing; national finalist in AB InBev's go-to-market challenge — 10 of 15,000 — on a $120M Gen-Z energy-drink brief.
- Startup stages: finalist at Collision (Canada) and Startup Istanbul with Vox Up, his first startup, a professional-networking platform.
- Boardrooms: 35+ C-level sessions to close a five-year, $1M ARR enterprise upsell with Jio (founder's office, Intellewings, 2025).
- Organiser's side: as Vice-President of his university's student council, he grew event participation 30% year on year.

## The record behind the talks

- Ninety-Eight Entertainment (founded 1 January 2020): started from a 300-sq-ft office in Delhi; the first client was a nightclub called Esquire; the first proper client was Pratima Singh, India basketball captain and Arjuna awardee, who introduced him to her husband, Ishant Sharma.
- Signed Ishant Sharma (100+ Tests for India) as exclusive talent in February 2022 — the same month as his ISB admit.
- Architected Ishant Sharma's RuPay × IPL 2022 partnership (300M+ impressions).
- Award-winning campaigns for Happy Dent and Borges; a hyperlocal influencer engine used by TrulyMadly and Slay Coffee; brand clients included Roseate and Hard Rock.
- Team of 18 across Delhi, Bombay and Bangalore; no outside funding.
- GMAT 760 (top 1%).
- Georgia Tech, 2019, at 19: visiting researcher under Dr Paul Yoder, programming GPUs in CUDA to linearise differential equations — 29% faster GPU computation. First in his family to leave the country.

## Bios

Poster line: Harsh Kumar Arya, founder of Ninety-Eight Entertainment, ISB MBA, and the talent manager who signed Ishant Sharma at 21.

Short bio (50 words): Harsh Kumar Arya is a Delhi NCR–based entrepreneur. He founded Ninety-Eight Entertainment in 2020 and bootstrapped it to ₹15 Cr+ in revenue, a team of eighteen and a roster that included cricketer Ishant Sharma, signed when Harsh was 21. Then he closed the agency at the top for an MBA at ISB.

Long bio (120 words): Harsh Kumar Arya is an entrepreneur from Ratlam, now based in Delhi NCR. In 2020 he founded Ninety-Eight Entertainment, a talent and marketing agency he bootstrapped to ₹15 Cr+ in revenue, eighteen people across three cities, 57 brand clients and a roster of 12 athletes and 500+ creators, including cricketer Ishant Sharma, signed exclusively when Harsh was 21. In 2023 he wound the agency down while it was still growing and went to the Indian School of Business, graduating with an MBA in 2025. A computer-science engineer and former Georgia Tech research scholar, he now runs Ninety-Eight 2.0, a creative-and-strategy practice for founders, helps run his family's school in the NCR, and co-writes GenZ Economics with Prof. Prasanna Tantri.

Emcee introduction (30 seconds): Our next speaker started trading pens at nine because his parents wouldn't buy him a thirty-five-rupee one. At twenty-one, he signed India fast bowler Ishant Sharma to his agency, Ninety-Eight Entertainment, which he grew to eighteen people across three cities without a rupee of outside funding. Then he closed it at the top and went to ISB. Please welcome Harsh Kumar Arya.

## Questions organisers ask

Q: Who is Harsh Kumar Arya?
A: An Indian entrepreneur and speaker based in Delhi NCR. He founded Ninety-Eight Entertainment in 2020 and bootstrapped it to ₹15 Cr+ in revenue, with a roster that included cricketer Ishant Sharma. He holds an MBA from the Indian School of Business (Class of 2025) and was a research scholar at Georgia Tech in 2019.

Q: What does he speak about?
A: Starting young, bootstrapping a company without investors, talent management and sports marketing, influencer and creator marketing, Gen-Z economics, and quitting well.

Q: Is he available for college fests and E-Cell events?
A: Yes. His talks are built for student audiences: college fests, E-Cells and entrepreneurship summits, orientations, B-schools, sports and media fests, and econ fests.

Q: Can he give a TEDx talk?
A: Yes. The ₹35 Pen and Close it at the top are written for the 18-minute TED-style format and for TEDx stages.

Q: Will he join a panel discussion or a fireside chat?
A: Yes. Panels and fireside chats are two of his five formats — entrepreneurship, marketing, the creator economy, sports business and Gen Z.

Q: Does he speak in Hindi?
A: Yes — English, Hindi, or a mix.

Q: Where is he based? Does he travel?
A: Delhi NCR; he travels anywhere with a stage and a working mic.

Q: What does he need on the day?
A: One mic, one clicker, and an introduction no longer than a line.

Q: What is his fee?
A: It depends on the format, city and date; include them when you write to hi@harsharya.com and the reply covers availability and terms.

Q: Is this the Harsh Arya who founded 98 Entertainment?
A: Yes. Harsh Kumar Arya founded Ninety-Eight (98) Entertainment, studied at ISB (Class of 2025) and Georgia Tech (2019), and was born in Ratlam, Madhya Pradesh. harsharya.com is his own site.
